newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas softens in Q3 but prompt and winter stab.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas softens in Q3 but prompt and winter stab.

text.p: Prices on the UK spot natural gas market softened in the third quarter on Wednesday, traders and brokers said, but other periods were relatively stable as the volume of trade picked up after a recent lull.

The third quarter traded at 11.00 pence and 11.10 pence a therm after being discussed in the range 11.25/11.40 pence a therm on Tuesday. The only Q3 deal seen done on Tuesday was index-related, making a price comparison difficult, but dealers agreed the market was softer. Bids by the close were heard at 10.95 pence a therm, breaking the psychologically important 11.00 pence barrier.

There was good interest in prompt material, the period which has seen most attention in the last few days, with prices seen largely stable. Trade was done between 11.30 pence and 11.50 pence on the day ahead, at 11.40 pence for the two days ahead, and at 11.50 pence for the first three days of June.
It was also rumoured that the whole month of June had traded twice, at 11.25 pence and 11.30 pence, although this was not confirmed by the close.

"June has softened a lot compared with other periods," said a trader, pointing out that it had been offered at 11.50 pence on Tuesday. By the close on Wednesday, he said, June was bid at 11.25 pence and offered at 11.30 pence, the levels at which it was also rumoured traded.
The April year was traded at least twice, at 13.45 pence and 13.475 pence. One counterparty in the deal at 13.45 pence said this indicated the stability in the market for outer periods.
"It's a little softer at the front but I really think it's unchanged further out. We've been talking the April year for days at the same price, and it's been done today," he said.

The winter also saw good activity, with trades seen for the Q4/Q1 strip, Q1 alone and the Q1/Q2 strip. Many traders appeared relieved to see volumes picking up after several days of minimal activity surrounding the bank holiday weekend.
But while the NBP was well traded, a St Fergus trader said the market there had been extremely quiet. "It's been very thin today, and we've had no enquiries at all at St Fergus," he said.

IPE futures were marked down in all periods, although the market only traded twice. Front-month June, which rolls on Thursday, and July were both traded at lower levels, but only the two deals were done for a total of 55 lots. One trader said it was not clear if futures were following or leading the physical market, and suggested it was a case of "the blind leading the blind."
